Summary

Stone Age – Gold Standard Begins
Paper money is backed by gold reserves. Governments can only print as much as they hold in gold.

World War I
Nations print excessive money to fund the war, breaking the gold standard for the first time.

Post-WWI Chaos
Europe is devastated. Debt, hyperinflation, and economic collapse destabilize nations and contribute to another global war.

After World War II (1945)
The U.S. emerges economically strong. The dollar is linked to gold, and global currencies are tied to the dollar, making it the center of world trade.

1945–1971
America prints more dollars to supply the growing global economy. Eventually printed more dollars than gold to backing them.

1971 – The Gold Window Closes
The U.S. ends the gold standard. The dollar is no longer backed by gold.

The Petrodollar Era
The U.S. partners with Saudi Arabia and OPEC. To price Oil in gold.
Now every country needs dollars to buy oil

Today
Countries like BRICS are trying to  bypass and Oil countries like Venezuela plays a role in the global power .

Will the dollar remain the world’s dominant currency or is a new system emerging?

Summary

Company
A company is like a basket of real things (trucks, tools) and invisible value (brand, trust).

0:00

Ownership
Stocks mean ownership. Bonds are loans with fixed returns.

Stocks vs Bonds
Bondholders get paid first but limited returns. Stockholders take more risk but keep the upside.

IPO
Companies sell pieces of ownership to raise money and grow.

Stock Market
Investors buy and sell shares between each other, not the company.

Why Invest
You earn through price growth or dividends.

Price Movement
Prices move based on supply, demand, and future expectations.

Strategy
Buy many companies (index funds) and hold long-term.
